newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Pemex details 11-mo crude exports, income. [CORRECTED 22:59 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Pemex details 11-mo crude exports, income. [CORRECTED 22:59 GMT]

text.p: Mexico's state-owned oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said Monday its crude exports from January to November averaged 1.55 million barrels per day (bpd), the same as the period January-October.

Export income totalled $9.69 billion, an increase of $2.89 billion for the time period compared with the first 11 months of 1995, because of higher global crude prices, the company said in a statement.

Through its sales unit, Petroleos Mexicanos International, Pemex said it sold an average 193,200 bpd of its light crude Isthmus, for a total $1.28 billion (corrects from million to billion and removes erroneous timeframe) in the first 11 months of the year.

The company said it exported about 866,300 bpd of heavy Maya crude, for a total $4.95 billion (corrects from million to billion and removes erroneous timeframe), and an average 487,900 bpd of extra-light Olmeca crude, for $3.46 billion (corrects from million to billion and removes erroneous timeframe), during the time period.
Average crude prices per barrel in the 11 months were $19.79 for Isthmus, $17.07 for Maya and $21.16 for Olmeca.

Of total exports in the time period, 77.9 percent were sold to the United States, eight percent to other countries in the Americas, 6.2 percent to Spain, 6.1 percent to the Far East and 1.8 percent to other countries in Europe.
